title: Choose a north star metric
summary: A north star metric captures the core value users get from the product. Paired with a few input metrics the team can influence, it keeps everyone pulling in the same direction.

beginner: Ask what value users get when the product works.
Find a number that reflects that value.
intermediate: Identify the moment users get real value and a metric that counts it.
Break it into three to five input metrics teams can move.
Check it reflects long-term value, not short-term spikes.
Align team goals to the inputs.
experienced: Run a workshop with leaders to agree the metric and inputs.
Check it cannot be gamed at the expense of users.
Use it to make prioritisation trade-offs across teams.
Know when to change it as the product matures.

canDelegateTo.task: Test candidate metrics against historical data

toolExamples.amplitude: Use the North Star template to map the metric and inputs.
toolExamples.looker: Define the metric once so every report uses it the same way.
toolExamples.miro: Draw the metric tree with inputs below the north star.

pitfalls: Choosing revenue, which measures value captured, not delivered
